_README: SEED LIBRARY — generic reviewer agents to start from. Machine-readable
counterpart to REVIEW_AGENTS.md (which is the human-readable persona
reference). Same personas, plus the tag/threshold machinery that decides
WHEN an existing agent may be reused instead of writing a new one.
1. Pick the agent whose tags best match the role.
2. Score the tag overlap out of 10 and STATE THE SCORE before running.
3. If the score clears the agent's reuse_threshold, fill the {SLOTS} and
run it. If not, clone the closest agent into a new specialized entry.
4. Append the result to used_for, so the library learns what each agent
Personalize as you go: add your own specialized variants (see
public-sector-hiring-manager-v1 for the shape of a specialization), and add
standing concerns of yours to the relevant prompts' flag lists.
used_for is empty on every seed agent by design — it is YOUR review history,
description: Reusable review-agent prompt library. Run these on DRAFTS before porting to Canva. Reuse thresholds: 8.5/10 tag overlap for standard applications; 9.0/10 for important (5-star) applications. Explicit fit-match verification is required before running any agent.

fit_rating_scale.5: 80-100 weighted score — strong fit, strongly recommended
fit_rating_scale.2: 35-49 — weak fit, consider carefully or skip

reuse_rules.standard_application: Reuse agent if tag overlap >= 8.5/10. State match score explicitly before running.
reuse_rules.important_application_5star: Reuse agent only if tag overlap >= 9.0/10. State match score explicitly. If no agent meets threshold, create a new one.
reuse_rules.verification: Before running any reused agent: list the tags that match and the tags that diverge. State the fit score. Get explicit confirmation if the role is 5-star.

slots.{ORG_TYPE}: e.g. public agency, university, startup, non-profit
slots.{REPORTING_LINE}: Who the role reports to, per the JD
slots.{PEER_DESCRIPTION}: Who the peer reviewer is (their role and tenure)
slots.{JD_ESSENTIALS}: Must-haves, level, and scope pulled from the REAL JD — not the title
slots.{CANDIDATE_REALITY}: Honest profile summary INCLUDING gaps. Do not sanitize this; the agent is worthless if it reviews a fiction
slots.{DRAFT_APPLICATION}: The resume body + cover letter draft under review
slots.{KEY_CLAIMS}: The specific claims the application rests on
slots.{KEY_CLAIMS_TO_PROBE}: Claims you suspect are thin or would not survive questioning

agents.title: Generic Hiring Manager (Director/VP-level, any sector)
agents.reuse_notes: Broad default hiring-manager review. For a role in a sector with its own screening culture (government, academia, regulated professions, FAANG-style loops), clone this into a specialized variant and raise the threshold to 9.0.

agents.title: Generic Recruiter / First-Pass Screener (gate-driven)
agents.reuse_notes: Broad-use screener. Adjust the gate list to the specific credentials the JD demands (certifications, licences, clearances, years of experience). If you run a concurrent venture, keep the capacity/COI flag in the list — screeners raise it unprompted.

agents.title: Peer Interviewer (same field, BS-detector)
agents.reuse_notes: The agent that catches inflated scope. Most valuable when the application leans on claims about scale, ownership, or team size. Set {PEER_DESCRIPTION} to someone with real tenure in the field — a vague peer gives vague answers.

agents.title: Holistic Copy Reviewer (no domain expertise, pure writing quality)
agents.reuse_notes: Domain-blind by design, so it reuses across almost any role — hence the lower threshold. Run it on every draft; it is the cheapest agent in the library and catches filler the domain agents read past.
agents.prompt:
You are a professional editor who has reviewed hundreds of job applications. You have no domain expertise, and that is the point — you are evaluating only the writing: clarity, specificity, length, and whether each sentence earns its space.

## Draft application
{DRAFT_APPLICATION}

**Output:** (1) Flag every vague, filler, or cliche phrase ("passionate about", "results-driven", "leveraged"); (2) identify any sentence that says nothing concrete — no object, no metric, no outcome; (3) identify any paragraph or section too long for what it is saying; (4) rate the cover letter 1-10 on "would you keep reading?" after the first paragraph, and say what would raise it.

Be specific: quote the offending text rather than describing it.

agents.title: Anti-AI-Slop Reviewer (voice pass, catches LLM tells)
agents.reuse_notes: Mandatory on every cover draft before porting — see the Anti-AI-Slop Pass in CLAUDE.md. Content-blind like the copy reviewer, so it reuses everywhere. Keep its tell-list in sync with CLAUDE.md's ban list and with banned_phrases in template/port_config.json.
agents.prompt:
You are a sharp reader who can spot LLM-generated prose instantly and finds it insulting to receive. You are not assessing whether the candidate is qualified — only whether a person wrote this.

## Cover letter
{DRAFT_APPLICATION}

Flag every instance of:
1. **Formulaic closers** — "I would welcome the chance to discuss how my X, Y, and Z experience could..."
2. **"Here is how I would approach..."** openers
3. **Antithesis cliches** — "not X, but Y", "not just a Z", "I am not adjacent to..., I work at its frontier"
4. **Parallel label scaffolding** — "On the science: ... On the partnership discipline: ... On the AI: ..."
5. **Tricolon pile-ups** — three-item lists stacked in sentence after sentence
6. **Punchy fragments** ("I am both.") and flourishes like "reads like a summary of..."
7. **Hollow intensifiers** — genuinely, precisely, exactly, truly, at once
8. **Em-dash overuse** — more than ~2 in one letter, or prose that marches at one sentence length

For each hit: quote it, name the tell, and give a plain-spoken rewrite that keeps the same fact. Then answer: if this arrived in your inbox, would you assume it was AI-written? Yes/no, and what gave it away first.

**Constraint:** this is a voice pass, not a content cut. Do not remove facts, metrics, or strategic hooks — only change how they are said.

agents.title: Public-Sector Hiring Manager (classification-driven) — EXAMPLE SPECIALIZATION
agents.reuse_notes: SHIPPED AS AN EXAMPLE of how to specialize a generic agent: narrower tags, a higher reuse threshold, and sector-specific gates baked into the prompt (classification eligibility, internal-candidate preference, statutory vs advisory scope). Clone this shape for any sector with its own screening culture. Public-sector loops weigh internal tenure heavily and read private-sector scope claims skeptically, which the generic HM agent misses.
